title: NodeKit build evidence pack
description: BUILD-stage handoff of the Builder Journey. Answers: which OpportunityContract decisions were honoured, which were defaulted-with-disclosure, and which were contradicted; what was built; and what GENERATED evidence supports each claim. Consumed by StoryPack and LaunchManifest. The root envelope is frozen by docs/JOURNEY_INTERSTAGE_CONTRACT.md and is not this schema's to change.

inputs.$comment: Every upstream artifact consumed. sha256 is over canonical JSON of the upstream document (keys sorted at every level, no insignificant whitespace). A stage that cannot produce the digest of what it consumed has been handed a name, not an artifact.

not.$comment: Redundant with additionalProperties:false, kept for a legible failure message. Self-approval is forbidden at authoring time; these are derived by verification from an attestation, never accepted as input.

utcDateTime.$comment: UTC only, matching nodeagent.event.v1. Offsets are rejected so two artifacts in one journey cannot disagree about ordering by timezone.

repoPath.$comment: Repository-relative POSIX path. No absolute paths, no traversal, no backslashes: an evidence path must resolve to the same bytes on any machine that has the repository.

jsonPointer.$comment: RFC 6901 pointer into the bound OpportunityContract, e.g. /wedge or /rejectedAlternatives/2 or /authorityLimits/prohibited/0.

evidenceRefs.$comment: Every reference must resolve to an entry in content.evidence. Resolution is the verifier's job; the schema only makes the reference mandatory and non-empty. A disposition without evidence is an assertion, and assertions are the failure mode this pack exists to prevent.

completeness.$comment: Frozen by the inter-stage contract. notRun is never empty merely because filling it was inconvenient: an empty notRun is a positive claim that everything in scope was attempted.

artifactRef.$comment: An artifact that exists on disk. path + sha256 + byteLength, never a boolean. `exists: true` is not evidence that anything exists.

evidence.$comment: The generation record for one artifact. There is deliberately no `kind: assertion` and no `passed`/`ok`/`verified` boolean: the only way to enter this array is to name a process that ran and the bytes it left behind.

observation.$comment: What the bytes show, stated so a reader who opens the artifact can agree or disagree. Not a verdict.

boundary.$comment: What this artifact does NOT establish. The anti-vacuous-pass field: evidence with no stated limit is evidence whose limit was never considered.

then.$comment: A test run without the command and its exit code is a claim that a test ran.

generation.$comment: How the artifact came to exist. `method` has no value meaning 'stated by the author', which is the point.

tool.$comment: The executable or module that produced the bytes, e.g. 'node --test' or 'src/lib/foo.mjs'.

actor.$comment: Who ran it. Recorded so a later reader can weigh self-produced evidence differently from independently produced evidence. It is metadata, never an approval.

disposition.$comment: EXACTLY three values, and every one of them is an admission. There is no 'not-applicable', no 'unknown', no null, and no way to omit the field: a decision that was neither honoured, disclosed, nor contradicted cannot be expressed. This is the whole point of the reconciliation — trial 1 shipped ten silent product decisions, and silence was expressible.

then.$comment: A default is only 'with disclosure' if the disclosure text exists AND an artifact contains it. whyNotEscalated forces the producer to say why it decided instead of asking — the exact move that went unrecorded ten times in trial 1.
A contradiction may be reported; it may never be self-approved. reportedIn must resolve to an artifact a human reads. There is deliberately no `approvedBy` here.

collectionDecisionEntry.$comment: For contract fields that are arrays. declaredElementCount is a claim about the bound upstream artifact that the verifier checks against the sha256'd OpportunityContract — reconciling 2 of 4 inputs now requires stating a count that is falsifiable, rather than silently covering the field with one word.

emergentDecision.$comment: A decision invented during BUILD that the OpportunityContract never mentions. This is where trial 1 actually failed: the ten silent decisions had no contract counterpart, so a contract-shaped reconciliation alone would have reported clean.

question.$comment: The open question as it stood before the choice. Written as a question, so a reader can tell it was a fork and not a foregone conclusion.

alternativesConsidered.$comment: At least one. A decision with no alternative was not a decision; it was a description.

authorityBucket.$comment: Which OpportunityContract.authorityLimits bucket this decision fell into. A value of 'approve' or 'prohibited' is the loud case: the build acted where it held no standing authority.

disclosedIn.$comment: The artifact where a human is actually told. A disclosure that exists only in this pack was disclosed to nobody.

then.$comment: Acting beyond `propose` requires stating the cost of undoing it. The producer still may not mark it approved.

emergentSweep.$comment: Absence of finding requires a search receipt. An empty `emergent` array is the claim that BUILD invented nothing, and that claim is only checkable if the producer states how and where it looked. Same logic as an empty notRun.

decisions.$comment: Two arms, because silence has two shapes: failing to reconcile a decision the contract made (contract), and failing to surface a decision the build made (emergent).

contractReconciliation.$comment: Closed enumeration of every decision-bearing field of nodekit.opportunity-contract/v1. `required` plus `additionalProperties:false` is the strongest lever JSON Schema offers: omitting `wedge` is a validation error rather than a quiet gap, and inventing a field the contract never had is also an error. Thirteen reconciliations are mandatory.

successCondition.$comment: The most gameable entry in the pack. A verifier should additionally require that at least one of its evidenceRefs names an evidence entry of kind `measurement` or `test-run`, which the schema cannot express because it cannot resolve ids.

rejectedAlternatives.$comment: `contradicted` here means the build implemented something the contract explicitly rejected.

surface.$comment: Something that now exists and can be pointed at. Existence is shown by source files with digests, never by a `built: true`.

identifier.$comment: How a user or agent reaches it: a route path, a command line, an exported symbol.

servesPointer.$comment: Optional pointer into the OpportunityContract this surface serves, so StoryPack can walk contract to surface without re-deriving the mapping.

surfaces.$comment: May legitimately be empty when BUILD refused everything — in which case completeness.refused carries the reasons. An empty surfaces array with an empty refused array is a pack that claims to have built nothing for no reason.

invocation.$comment: How LaunchManifest starts the thing. Present so the next stage does not have to guess an entrypoint.

requiredEnv.$comment: Variable NAMES only. Values are secrets and never belong in a committed artifact.

claim.$comment: A statement StoryPack may repeat to a human. Each one carries its own evidence and its own stated limit, so an unbindable claim is visible here rather than discovered downstream.

boundary.$comment: What the cited evidence does not establish. Required, because a claim whose limits were never written down is a claim nobody bounded.

summary.$comment: One paragraph a human reads first. It is an index into the rest, not a substitute for it.

evidence.$comment: The generated-artifact pool every other section refers into. evidenceId uniqueness is not expressible in JSON Schema (uniqueItems compares whole items) and is a verifier obligation.

promotionAuthorized.$comment: Pinned false. A producer may write false and never true; the true value is derived by verification from an attestation. The field exists rather than being omitted so that its absence cannot be read as authorization.
